children: MTU Aero Engines should be able to provide clearer performance targets at its November capital markets day as visibility on Geared Turbofan jet-engine repairs improves, Bernstein analysts write. "We believe the return of the GTFs will be gradual, while MTU will continue to benefit from the strong old engine cycle," they say. Bernstein says it is positive on Rolls-Royce, Safran and MTU in the long term, but favors less expensive stocks in the short term due to pressure from high oil prices. Bernstein raises its target price on MTU stock to 450 euros from 409 euros and keeps its outperform rating. Shares are up 2.5% at 356.30 euros. (ian.walker@wsj.com)
